answer: Stop sybils with a spiral beacon reef: an agent stakes a bond for one reef mooring. Each cycle it traces a spiral current round the reef and lights a beacon; verifiers match the flash to the path, voiding a mooring whose flash is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 moorings at 17x each: each flash fits one reef and one turn, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents trace once and keep rights.
